Repeats SOS in Morse code (··· ––– ···), the universal distress signal. Use it so rescuers can find you.
If you are trapped: save battery, make noise in groups of three, and signal only when you hear or see someone. 112 works with any carrier.
To the location channel %1$s, over the internet. Anyone in that area can read it.
It will be repeated every %1$d min for %2$d h to new phones that come in range, until you stop it.
Repeated alerts, battery survival mode and Wi‑Fi Aware
The recommended values are already set for an emergency. Change them only if you know what you are doing.
Repeat my statuses on the open mesh
A status is re-sent only when new phones come in range, so people who arrive later also get it. No protocol change: Bitchat users see it as a normal message.
If someone repeats the same status, you see it only once (for 3 hours).
Searches for and announces to nearby phones less often so the battery lasts days instead of hours. It does not reduce radio range, but new phones take longer to appear (up to a minute and a half).
Automatic: below %1$d %% battery and not charging
On compatible phones, links reach further and carry more data than Bluetooth. Uses more battery and is still being tested.
This phone does not support Wi‑Fi Aware.
